title.rendered: My Help Comes from the Lord: Morning Devotional

excerpt.rendered: Where does your help come from? Saturday’s devotional on Psalm 121, the pilgrim’s song of the Lord who watches over your going out and coming in, from this time forth and forevermore.

content.rendered:
The Gospel For Today | Saturday, May 2, 2026

📖 Today’s Scripture

“I lift up my eyes to the mountains, where does my help come from? My help comes from the Lord, the Maker of heaven and earth.”
Psalm 121:1–2 (NIV) | ESV

📝 Today’s Message

The psalmist looks up at the mountains and asks the honest question that every person in difficulty eventually asks: where does my help come from? It is not a question born of doubt, it is a question already moving toward its answer. The asking is the beginning of the receiving.

And the answer arrives with stunning clarity: My help comes from the Lord. Not from the mountain. Not from the circumstances shifting. Not from the right person showing up or the right door opening. From the Lord, the Maker of heaven and earth. The One who spoke the mountains into existence is the One who helps you.

The rest of Psalm 121 unpacks what that help looks like: He will not let your foot slip. He who watches over you will not slumber. He will keep you from all harm. He will watch over your coming and going, both now and forevermore. This is not vague comfort. It is specific, comprehensive, covenant protection.

In Philippians 4:19, Paul declares: “My God will meet all your needs according to the riches of his glory in Christ Jesus.” Not some needs. All needs. Your help comes from the Lord. And the Lord has no shortage of anything.

🙏 Prayer

Father, I lift my eyes to You today. My help does not come from circumstances, from people, or from my own ability to figure things out. My help comes from You, the Maker of heaven and earth, who lacks nothing and withholds nothing good from those who trust You. I trust You today. Meet every need according to Your riches in glory. In Jesus’ name. Amen.

🗣️ Declaration

My help comes from the Lord, the Maker of heaven and earth. He is my source. He does not sleep, He does not fail, and He does not run short. Every need I have is already known to Him and already provided for in Christ. I lift my eyes off my circumstances and fix them on my God. He watches over me. He keeps me. He helps me. Today, tomorrow, and forevermore.
